acceptance.slack_rule: After final v45 Git readback only, emit at most one sanitized version-advance pointer. Do not rewrite CURRENT merely to embed the Slack link.

experiment.controlled_factor: Keep event canonicalization, v3 semantic-core idempotency, event-first write/readback, exact second CURRENT read, and single-file blob-SHA guard fixed; vary only the carrier observation surface used to obtain the same task instruction body.
experiment.hypothesis: The visible task instruction body remains byte-equivalent after NFC plus LF normalization between the current scheduled-task invocation and the native task inventory prompt field, while surrounding runtime envelope metadata remains excluded from the object transition and idempotency key.
experiment.strongest_falsifier: The proposed idempotency key or v45 Slack token already exists; task ID differs; normalized instruction-body digests differ; CURRENT is not exact v44 on the second read; event digest recomputation fails; final CURRENT/event/predecessor bindings disagree; or Slack is posted before final Git readback.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This compares two observations exposed by the same provider and the same scheduled-task carrier, not distinct runtimes, vendors, models, accounts, or failure domains. The current invocation body was captured from the model-visible instruction text rather than a provider-signed raw-message export. Equality after the stated normalization does not prove hidden envelope equality, end-to-end transport integrity, or future replay equivalence. Git event creation, CURRENT replacement, validation reads, duplicate searches, and Slack posting remain separate effects. Git provides no cross-file atomicity, database isolation, linearizability, exactly-once execution, referential integrity, server-side idempotency uniqueness, Slack atomicity, lock fairness, or automatic orphan repair.
canonical_transition.rollback: Append a compensating event from the then-current version; never delete this event or Slack pointer; replace CURRENT only with its exact then-current blob SHA.
